title: Underlying tensor normalization of pro-etale scalar and inverse-image comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and an arbitrary morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$. Use the ordinary uncompleted unbounded small pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the exact identified-coefficient inverse images $L_R=f_R^*$ for $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and the canonical constant-ring maps $c_R:f^{-1}R_Y\simeq R_X$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Write $T_Z=(-)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Z}B_Z$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] and let $r_Z$ restrict scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] for $Z=X,Y$. Let $b:r_XL_B\simeq L_Ar_Y$ be the canonical restriction comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], and let $\theta:L_BT_Y\simeq T_XL_A$ be the canonical coefficient/pullback comparison [def-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-comparison]. Let $\tau_K:L_A(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Y}B_Y)\simeq L_AK\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}B_X$ be the canonical tensor/pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], using $c_B$ on the coefficient factor. Under $r_ZT_ZK=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Z}B_Z$, one has, naturally for every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$,
$$r_X(\theta_K)\circ b_{T_YK}^{-1}=\tau_K.$$
More precisely, for every flat-term K-flat cochain complex $P$ of $A_Y$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the left-hand comparison at $K=QP$ is represented, through the canonical scalar-derived counits and the exact inverse-image and restriction localization factor maps, by the chain isomorphism
$$t_P:f_A^*r_Y(P\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}r_X(f_A^*P\otimes_{A_X}B_X).$$
Here tensor means the sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and scalar restriction on complexes is termwise. In degree $i$, for an object $V$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and sections $x\in P^i(V)$ and $s\in B_Y(V)$, the map sends the inverse-image unit section of $x\otimes s$ to the tensor of the inverse-image unit section of $x$ and $c_B(f^{-1}s)$ on $X\times_YV$. No boundedness of $P$ or $K$, and no flatness or finite Tor dimension of $B$ over $A$, is required.
